move.headline: A small gain after a huge run

evidence.t: Dell rose 0.86% while the S&P 500 fell 0.22%. A typical day for Dell moves about 5% (last 60 trading days), so this is well inside its normal range and no classification is triggered.
Peers fell too: HPE −1.4%, Super Micro −1.1%, HP Inc −2.0%, NetApp −1.1%, Celestica −1.2% on the day.
Shares are up 28.8% over 3 months and stand 93% above their 200-day average after the 1 Sep results and guidance raise.

past.date: Tue 1 Sep 2026, after the US close (Wed 2 Sep, about 4am Singapore)
past.vs: Revenue $47.0bn, +58% vs a year earlier, vs $44.95bn expected (+4.5%). Non-GAAP EPS $7.04 vs $4.91 expected (+43%).
past.guide: October quarter: revenue about $49.0bn (+81% vs a year earlier) vs $41.43bn expected; non-GAAP EPS $6.50 vs $4.49 expected. Full year FY27 raised to $192bn revenue (from $167bn) and $74bn of AI server revenue (from about $60bn).
past.reaction: Shares fell 6.8% on results day (1 Sep, to $425.0), then rose 15.8% the next day ($425.0 to $492.2) and 25.6% over four sessions to $533.88 (8 Sep), each measured against the 1 Sep close.
take: AI orders exploded. $60.9bn of AI server orders in the quarter (a record), $16.4bn shipped, backlog $95bn.
Margins rose, not fell. Gross margin 20.9% vs 17.7% the quarter before; ISG operating margin 15.0% vs 8.8% a year earlier.
PCs are growing again. Commercial PCs +22% and storage +26% vs a year earlier: growth beyond AI.
Supply, not demand, is the limit. COO Jeff Clarke: 'DRAM, DRAM, DRAM followed by NAND, NAND, NAND. We have spotty CPU shortages.'
Cash lagged profit. Operating cash $2.2bn vs $4.1bn net income in the quarter; inventories $21.3bn vs $10.4bn at end-January 2026 as AI orders are built.
$4.3bn returned in the quarter: $3.8bn buybacks plus dividends.
past.impact: Guidance far above expectations (DM3 bullish); AI orders (DM4a), PCs (DM4b) and storage (DM4c) all bullish; forecasts revised up sharply (DM2).

past.reaction: Shares +33% the next day ($317.0 to $420.9; best day ever, CNBC).
take: AI servers took over. $16.1bn of AI server revenue, +757% vs a year earlier; orders $24.4bn; backlog $51.3bn.
Traditional servers +92% and storage +8% vs a year earlier.
Memory costs forced fast repricing of PCs, servers and storage (COO Jeff Clarke).
5,000+ AI customers, widening beyond a few large AI clouds.

watch: Revenue vs the ~$49bn guide; AI server revenue vs the ~$20.7bn a quarter that the $74bn full-year AI guide implies for the second half (vs $16.4bn in the July quarter).

lead: Dell is Building history (today's zone: Buy), unchanged at +36 on a −100 to +100 scale as of 7 Oct (also +36 on 6 Oct and 5 Oct), just 6 points above the Hold line: the share price rose 0.86% on the day vs −0.22% for the S&P 500, but no bucket score moved, so the call stays driven by exceptional AI-driven demand against a stretched price and a valuation well above its hardware peers.
bullets: Demand is exceptional. Demand scores +76: revenue grew 57.7% in the July quarter vs a year earlier, well above the 39.2% average of the prior four quarters; AI server orders over the last two quarters were +382% vs the same two quarters a year earlier ($85.3bn vs $17.7bn); October-quarter guidance (+81.4% vs a year earlier) beat what analysts expected (+53.4%) by 28 points; analysts' profit forecast for the year to Jan 2028 rose 34.4% in 90 days; Taiwan AI-server makers' sales were +96.8% (Jun-Aug vs a year earlier). Soft spot: gross margin over the last 4 quarters was 19.8% vs 21.1% a year earlier, as lower-margin AI servers grow.

It is expensive vs its hardware peers. Valuation scores −44 (unchanged): investors pay 23.1x expected next-12-month profit vs a 13.0x peer median (+77%), EV/EBITDA is 22.1x vs 14.3x (+55%), and trailing P/E is 33.7x vs Dell's own 5-year median of 21.5x (+57%). Only the growth-adjusted P/E looks cheap (0.6 vs a 1.0 peer median, −42%), and that rests on long-term growth forecasts: analysts expect slightly lower earnings per share in the year to Jan 2028 ($24.66) than this year ($25.90).

Money flows are mixed. Liquidity scores +13 (unchanged): volume on up days was 1.40x volume on down days over the last 20 trading days (bullish), but institutions cut a net 2.38 points of shares last quarter (Jun 30 filings) and the dollar index rose 2.99 points in 20 trading days (both bearish).

The price trend is strong but stretched. Price trend scores +72 (unchanged): at $578.96 (+0.86% on the day vs −0.22% for the S&P 500) the stock is 93% above its 200-day average and the 50-day average is 66% above the 200-day; over 3 months it is 3.4 points behind its peers (neutral; it turns bearish at 5 points behind; it was 0.7 behind yesterday).

Fragile and not confirmed. Day 3 of 10 trading days of history; the call is confirmed after 7 of 10 days in one zone. One indicator moving (growth-adjusted P/E turning neutral, or relative strength vs peers turning bearish) would take the score below +30, into Hold. Watch: cash lagging profit (free cash flow $986m in the July quarter vs $1,868m a year earlier), about $1.03bn of insider and Silver Lake share sales in 6 months with no buying, and the 10-year yield (5.28%, +0.44 points in 20 trading days).
defects: Staging build, third day of history: the call needs 7 of 10 trading days in one zone before it is confirmed.
Valuation vs own history (VL3) uses trailing P/E: free forward P/E history is too short.
DM3, DM4a-c and DM5 are typed in from Dell's results and the Taiwan exchange, so they update quarterly (DM5 monthly).
Holder percentages use all ~636m shares (Class A, B and C), not the 315m tradable Class C shares.
Lenovo (peer) is priced in HKD but reports in USD; its EV/EBITDA is excluded and its P/E may be distorted (Framework chat item).
Yahoo shows the VMware spin-off (1 Nov 2021) as a 1.973-for-1 split; older SEC EPS is divided by 1.973 to match.
Chain C2 has no live watch number until the Framework chat adds CoreWeave to the shared data.

AI servers are described in the text, not shown as their own part, until then.
Two peers (Lenovo, Quanta) trade in Asia: their prices are taken from the Asian session running when the page is built, not the US close (relative strength PT4 reads −3.4 vs a −5 line).

Growth-adjusted P/E (VL2) uses Yahoo's PEG (0.58), which does not show its growth basis; analysts' EPS for the year to Jan 2028 ($24.66) is below this year's ($25.90), so the 'cheap after growth' reading rests on longer-term growth forecasts.

SRV.sells: Servers and networking: AI-optimized servers (GPU racks, $16.4bn in the July quarter, 35% of Dell's revenue) and traditional servers ($10.5bn, 22%).
SRV.buyers: AI cloud providers ('neoclouds'), AI labs, large companies and governments.
pos: The growth engine: AI servers +100% and traditional servers +122% in the July quarter vs a year earlier.
Backed by a $95bn AI order backlog (1 Sep 2026), about two quarters of total company revenue.
ISG's operating margin rose to 15.0% from 8.8% a year earlier as volume grew.
neg: Not recurring: big, lumpy deals that can slip between quarters.
Concentrated in a small number of very large AI buyers whose funding depends on debt markets (chain C2).
Depends on Nvidia's GPU supply and memory prices (chains C1, C5).

STO.sells: Data storage systems (all-flash arrays, file and object storage).
STO.buyers: Companies and governments; increasingly for AI data.
pos: Usually one of Dell's higher-margin hardware lines (Dell does not report storage margin separately), so growth here helps profit more than its size suggests.
+26% in the July quarter vs a year earlier, after −1% in the Oct 2025 quarter.
neg: Shrinking share: 11.9% of revenue over the last 4 quarters vs 16.3% a year earlier, as servers grow faster.

COM.sells: PCs, laptops and monitors for businesses.
pos: Growing again: +22% in the July quarter vs a year earlier (PC upgrade cycle).
A steady, diversified customer base that does not depend on AI.
neg: Low margin: CSG earns about 6.6% operating margin (last 4 quarters) vs ISG's 13.2%.
Memory price rises force PC price increases that can dent demand (chain C1).

CON.sells: PCs and laptops for consumers (incl. Alienware gaming).
pos: Small (about 4% of revenue), so swings matter little.
+7% in the July quarter vs a year earlier.
neg: Long decline: share of revenue fell from about 10% to under 5% in 3 years.
Most price-sensitive part of Dell; memory-driven price rises hit it first.

shift.title: What the shift means for Dell
pos: Servers (mostly AI) rose from 20% of revenue (4 quarters to Jan 2024) to 51% (4 quarters to Jul 2026; 57% in the July 2026 quarter alone), turning Dell from a PC company into an AI infrastructure company.
Profit followed: operating profit $5.4bn in the July quarter vs $1.8bn a year earlier (SEC); ISG margin rose with scale.
neg: Lower-margin mix: AI servers earn less per dollar than storage and services, so company gross margin is structurally lower than before (20.0% in FY26 vs 23.8% in FY24, SEC).
More concentrated and more cyclical: a pause in AI spending would hit a much larger share of Dell's revenue than before.
